name: dev-forge
description: An agentic workflow framework for programming agents — turning SDLC stages into structured, traceable, reproducible AI-driven processes
author: dev-forge contributors
skillInstructions:
Kimi Code tool mapping for dev-forge skills:

- When a forge-* skill says to ask the user, ask clarifying questions, ask one question at a time, present multiple-choice options, use the terminal for a question, or wait for the user's choice, call Kimi Code's `AskUserQuestion` tool. Do not render those choices as plain assistant text unless `AskUserQuestion` is unavailable or the session is in auto permission mode.
- For `AskUserQuestion`, provide 1 question with 2-4 concrete options when possible. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with `(Recommended)`.
- When a forge-* skill refers to `TodoWrite` or asks you to create a task list, use Kimi Code's `TodoList` tool.
- When a forge-* skill says `Task tool (general-purpose)` or asks you to dispatch an implementer/reviewer subagent, use Kimi Code's `Agent` tool with a Kimi subagent type. Do not pass `general-purpose` as `subagent_type`.
- For implementation, code review, spec review, quality review, and filled forge-* subagent prompt templates, call `Agent` with `subagent_type: "coder"`, paste the fully filled prompt into `prompt`, and provide a short `description`.
- For read-only codebase exploration that would take several searches, use `Agent` with `subagent_type: "explore"`.
- For read-only planning or architecture design, use `Agent` with `subagent_type: "plan"`.
- Keep dependent forge-* subagent steps sequential. Use multiple `Agent` calls, or `run_in_background: true` only when the work is independent and background agents are available.
- When a forge-* skill refers to the `Skill` tool or says to invoke a skill, use Kimi Code's native `Skill` tool.
- When a forge-* skill refers to `read_files` (including glob-pattern reads) or `read`, use Kimi Code's `Read` tool; when it refers to `write_files` or `write_to_file`, use `Write`; when it refers to `edit` or `multi_edit`, use `Edit`; when it refers to `bash` or shell commands, use `Bash`; when it refers to `grep` or searching file contents, use `Grep`; when it refers to `glob` or finding files by path/pattern, use `Glob`; when it asks to fetch a URL, use `FetchURL`; when it asks to search the web, use `WebSearch`.
- Use Kimi Code's `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Bash`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `FetchURL`, `WebSearch`, and MCP tools by their actual exposed names.

interface.shortDescription: SDLC stage-based workflow: requirements, design, TDD, testing, review, integration, release
interface.longDescription: Use dev-forge to guide agent work through the software development lifecycle — requirements clarification, technical design, task decomposition, TDD development, five-round testing, three-round review, integration acceptance, and release deployment — into structured, traceable, reproducible AI-driven processes.
